::: {.hero-right}
I have worked at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health (BSPH) for about seven years, and I am currently a **Faculty Research Associate in the Department of Mental Health**. I serve as **lead biostatistician and data scientist** on multidisciplinary research into substance use, substance use disorders, and behavioral health at the [Thrul Lab](https://www.thrulresearchlab.com/). This work sits where public health, data science, biostatistics, psychology, and health informatics meet. My focus is **addiction and overdose prevention**, along with **mental and digital health**.

I work across the full research lifecycle. I collaborate on study design, recruit participants through social media campaigns, and build and test data-collection infrastructure. I also randomize participants across study arms, and I manage, analyze, and interpret complex datasets. Much of this work uses digital technology to understand and address substance use. With **ecological momentary assessment (EMA)** and **micro-randomized trial** designs, we capture people's behaviors and experiences in real time and test interventions in real-world settings. My data sources also include cross-sectional surveys, prospective cohorts, randomized trials, wearables, smartphone GPS, and electronic health records.
